mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters indicates a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of quarters with positive GDP growth, or GDP growth and SPX returns show a negative correlation over a 5-year period (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals an improving labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and confidence increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decrease and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production over two consecutive months signals increased economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of months with positive INDPRO growth, or INDPRO growth and SPX returns show a negative correlation over a 3-year period (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% in a month signals a strengthening housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between HOUST increase and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and CPI is increasing by more than 0.5% month-over-month, the combination signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, typically leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with high interest rates
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3%, the combination signals a robust labor market, typically leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and confidence increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real GDP by more than 1% in a quarter signals an economic contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer spending decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 40% of quarters with negative GDP growth, or GDP contraction and SPX returns show a positive correlation over a 3-year period (p < 0.05).
